precepts.text: Though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, cuz all the glory goes back to the father. Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up so they can repent. Woe is unto us if we preach not the gospel. We got to do this thing willingly; nobody can force you. If you do it willingly, you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. But if against your will, he going to take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside them doors in the midst of wickedness again.
precepts.point: And now we be here praying for you.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
The prayer is that God would “give you all an heart to serve him, and to do his will, with a good courage and a willing mind.” If you want to return, if you want to repent, he will give you a heart to serve him and to keep his law and commandments. And it must be with a willing mind. Paul shows what that means.

“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of”: though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, because all the glory goes back to the Father. “For necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up, so they can repent, come out of it, and cast away their iniquities. Woe unto us if we preach not the gospel.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” We have to do this thing willingly. Nobody can force you. If you do it willingly you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. “But if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” If you do it against your will, he will take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside those doors in the midst of wickedness and evil again.

So we have to serve the Lord with a willing mind, a sincere heart, and loyalty. We have to come out of all the wickedness we learned here in America, from under the hypnosis given to us here, and serve him willingly.

precepts.text: Behold, the Lord's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: but your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear. Your sins is the only thing that separates you from your God. If you doing what you supposed to do, keeping the law of commandments in the faith of Christ, he going to come to you, send you peace, and hear your prayers.
precepts.point: And now we be here praying for you.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
The prayer asks God to “send you peace, And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.” You wonder why you have no peace in your life right now, why you are all over the place? Because you are not serving him, not keeping his law and commandments in sincerity. Isaiah shows what keeps us from being one with God.

“Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save.” His hand is not so short that he can’t reach down and help you when you are afflicted or in trouble. “Neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear.” His ear is not so heavy that he can’t hear your prayers and your cries and come down and get you out of that situation.

“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” That is what separates you from your God: your sins, your iniquities. That is the only way he separates himself from you, if you are in the midst of sin.

But if you are doing what you are supposed to do, keeping the law of commandments in the faith of Christ, he is going to come to you, send you peace, and hear your prayers. If you are sincere and honest with him, walking right in his sight, waking up and returning to him, he will never forsake you in time of trouble. He will help you through your hard times.

points: And give you all a what? An heart to serve him. The Lord has been gracious unto us because he gave us our heart and understanding to serve him. Do you understand that we understand what the will of God is? People will spend a whole lifetime in church and don't know that Christ is black. I don't even understand how you don't know that in 2026. That you have to keep the commandments. That you can't eat pork. That a woman can't wear pants. Those are very basic things. But God was gracious to us, that we know what his will is. So read that verse again. Verse three.

With a what? A willing mind. That's the sincere. A willing mind. You have to want to do this. Brothers wonder why they're not growing, because it's not important to them. This is not the apple of their eye. So when it's time to sit down and go through prophecies, it'd be way over your head. You can't understand basic things like reading four chapters a day. You have to have a willing spirit to do this. We are where we at because us collectively, men, we understand that. That's how we're able to grow personally and congregationally. All of us for the most part is doing this part-time. We all have jobs. But for the ones that's serious, that have a willing mind, they on them streets. They out there putting their labour in.

Notice what it says. He opens your heart in his law and commandments and send you peace. Those are all in conjunction. So if you want peace in your life, in this truth, in your marriage, in your friendship, you have to have a willing mind to come and serve God. He said this is the rest where it would rest, to bring you peace. So the Lord is gracious to us to show us who we are, what the will of God is, and it has to be important to you. Read on.
